title: Breton Buckwheat Galettes with Smoked Salmon, Dill & Crème Fraîche
dek: Lacy buckwheat galettes folded around cool smoked salmon, lemony crème fraîche, capers and fresh dill make an elegant but practical skillet brunch.
image_alt: Folded brown buckwheat galettes topped with smoked salmon, crème fraîche, fresh dill and lemon wedges on white plates
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups (180 g) buckwheat flour, preferably finely milled
2 cups cold water, plus 2 to 4 tbsp as needed
2 tbsp unsalted butter, melted and cooled, plus more for the skillet
10 oz refrigerated cold-smoked salmon, separated into ribbons
1/3 cup loosely packed fresh dill fronds

instructions.name: Whisk the buckwheat batter
instructions.text: Whisk the buckwheat flour and salt in a large bowl. In a second bowl, whisk the egg with 2 cups cold water, then slowly whisk the liquid into the flour until smooth. Whisk in the 2 tablespoons melted butter. The batter should pour like light cream; add 2 to 4 tablespoons more water if it falls from the whisk in thick ribbons.

instructions.name: Rest and recheck the consistency
instructions.text: Cover and rest the batter at room temperature for 30 minutes so the flour hydrates and the bubbles settle. Keep the smoked salmon refrigerated during the rest. Whisk the batter again; if it has thickened, add cold water 1 tablespoon at a time until it flows readily across a tilted skillet.

instructions.name: Make the lemon crème fraîche
instructions.text: Stir the crème fraîche, lemon juice, lemon zest and black pepper in a small bowl. Refrigerate until assembly. Set out the salmon, capers, dill and lemon wedges only when the skillet is ready so the seafood stays cold.

instructions.name: Heat and butter the skillet
instructions.text: Heat a 10-inch nonstick or well-seasoned carbon-steel skillet over medium for 2 minutes. Brush it with a very thin film of butter. The pan is ready when a drop of batter sizzles immediately without smoking; lower the heat if the butter browns before the batter is added.

instructions.name: Cook the first side
instructions.text: Whisk the batter, pour a scant 1/3 cup into the center and immediately tilt and rotate the skillet to spread it into a thin 9-inch round. Cook for 60 to 90 seconds, until the surface looks dry, the edges lift and the underside is mottled brown. There should be no glossy wet batter remaining.

instructions.name: Flip and finish the galette
instructions.text: Slide a thin spatula underneath, flip and cook the second side for 30 to 45 seconds. Transfer to a parchment-lined sheet pan and cover loosely with a clean towel. Repeat with the remaining batter, brushing the skillet lightly with butter as needed, to make 8 galettes. Adjust the heat rather than letting the pan smoke.

instructions.name: Fold and garnish
instructions.text: Return one galette to the warm skillet for 15 seconds. Fold four sides inward to form an open square and transfer to a plate. Top with about 1 1/2 tablespoons lemon crème fraîche, 1 1/4 ounces smoked salmon, capers and dill. Repeat, serving 2 galettes per person with a lemon wedge. Do not leave the smoked salmon at room temperature for more than 2 hours total.

why_it_works: A short rest fully hydrates buckwheat flour, which makes the egg-bound batter easier to spread thinly without tearing at the edges.
A properly preheated skillet sets the batter on contact, creating the lacy browned surface and crisp rim visible on a Breton-style galette.
Cool smoked salmon and lemony crème fraîche are added after cooking, preserving their silky textures while capers, dill and fresh lemon balance the rich fish.
swaps: For a dairy-free version, cook with neutral oil and replace crème fraîche with a thick unsweetened dairy-free yogurt mixed with the lemon juice and zest.
Replace cold-smoked salmon with flaked freshly cooked salmon. Cook the fish to 145°F, cool promptly, then refrigerate before assembling the galettes.

If strict gluten-free cooking is required, use certified gluten-free buckwheat flour and verify the smoked salmon and all packaged ingredients; buckwheat itself is naturally gluten-free, but cross-contact is possible.
storage: Cool unfilled galettes completely, layer them with parchment and refrigerate airtight for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Refrigerate the lemon crème fraîche for up to 3 days and follow the smoked-salmon package date after opening. Rewarm galettes one at a time in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 20 to 30 seconds per side, then add the cold toppings. Refrigerate assembled leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day; their edges will soften.
notes: Keep refrigerated smoked salmon at 40°F or below and return it to the refrigerator between batches; discard perishable food left out longer than 2 hours, or 1 hour when the room is above 90°F.

Refrigerated smoked seafood is a higher-risk ready-to-eat food for pregnant, older or immunocompromised diners. For those guests, use freshly cooked salmon cooled under refrigeration instead of cold-smoked salmon.
The batter contains egg, so cook every galette until both sides are set and no glossy wet batter remains.
A low-sided crepe pan is convenient but not required; a 10-inch nonstick or well-seasoned carbon-steel skillet works well.

faqs.q: Why does my buckwheat galette tear when I flip it?
faqs.a: The batter may be too thick, the pan may be too cool or the first side may not be fully set. Thin the batter 1 tablespoon at a time, let the skillet reheat and wait until the entire surface looks dry and the edges release before flipping.

faqs.q: Can I make the batter the night before?
faqs.a: Yes. Cover and refrigerate it for up to 24 hours, then bring it toward room temperature for 15 minutes and whisk well. Add cold water a tablespoon at a time if the chilled batter has thickened.

faqs.q: Do I need a special galette pan or wooden spreader?
faqs.a: No. A 10-inch nonstick or seasoned carbon-steel skillet and a thin spatula are enough. Pour the batter into the center and rotate the skillet immediately; a wooden rozell is useful for a large flat griddle but awkward in a home skillet.
